alphaScore.title: Alpha Score
alphaScore.overallTooltip: Weighted mix of 6 metrics (0-100): Profit Factor 25%, Recovery Factor 20%, Max Drawdown 20%, Consistency 15%, Win Rate 10%, Avg Win/Loss Ratio 10%. Risk & consistency together account for 55%, raw hit rate only 45% — a high score reflects sustainable, controlled performance rather than just a lot of winning trades.
alphaScore.provisionalTitle: Only {count}/{total} closed trades — score still statistically uncertain
alphaScore.axisWinRateTooltip: Share of winning trades (weighting 10%). 30% or less = 0 points, 70% or more = 100 points. Rises with every winning trade, falls with every losing trade. For strategies with a high reward-risk ratio, a low win rate is normal and not a warning sign.
alphaScore.axisProfitFactorTooltip: Gross profit ÷ gross loss (weighting 25%, the single most important metric). PF 0.5 or less = 0 points, PF 3.0 or more = 100 points. Captures hit rate and risk-reward ratio together — every trade directly affects it.
alphaScore.axisAvgWinLossTooltip: Ratio of average win to average loss (weighting 10%). 1:1 = 33 points, 3:1 or more = 100 points. Rises when winners are on average larger than losers, e.g. through trailing stops or cutting losses early.
alphaScore.axisRecoveryTooltip: Recovery Factor = net profit ÷ largest drawdown in € (weighting 20%). Shows how well the account recovers from losing phases. RF 0 = 0 points, RF 3 or more = 100 points. Worsens with deep drawdowns, improves with steady profit growth.
alphaScore.axisMaxDrawdownTooltip: Largest decline from the account's prior high, in percent (weighting 20%). 0% drawdown = 100 points, 20% drawdown or more = 0 points. Any losing streak that creates a new low below the last high permanently worsens this value.
alphaScore.axisConsistencyTooltip: Share of profitable trading days out of all trading days (weighting 15%). A day counts as profitable if the sum of all trades on that day is positive. Many individual losing days worsen this value, even if the overall balance is positive.
